stories.title: Biotechnology shifts focus from research to solutions
stories.summary: Biological sciences are moving beyond traditional laboratory research toward applied technologies like data science and bioengineering. The shift aims to translate scientific knowledge into practical solutions for quality of life. Modern discoveries are increasingly focused on vaccines, molecular diagnostics, and genomic tools to address contemporary health and societal needs.

stories.title: Indian students weigh job prospects over university rankings
stories.summary: Indian students are increasingly prioritizing post-graduation job markets and costs when choosing overseas universities. With approximately 8 lakh students currently enrolled abroad, outbound mobility is projected to grow by 4 percent annually. Academic excellence is no longer the sole driver for students navigating tighter visa policies and currency fluctuations.

stories.title: Visa hurdles shift student interest from US to Europe
stories.summary: Uncertainty in the US IT job market and tightening visa rules are prompting students from Telangana and Andhra Pradesh to consider alternatives. Nations including the UK, Germany, Ireland, and New Zealand are emerging as preferred destinations. Students are now being urged to evaluate future prospects and fees more carefully.

stories.title: Studying abroad remains a life goal despite risks
stories.summary: For decades, studying abroad has been a primary life goal for students in India, particularly in states with large IT sectors. While the US, UK, Canada, and Australia remain popular, the path to settling in a foreign country has become increasingly complex for those seeking greener pastures.

stories.title: Canadian study permits for Indian students hit decade low
stories.summary: Study permits held by Indian students in Canada are on track for their lowest level in over a decade. Data from Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada shows 51,900 Indian permit holders as of September 30, 2026. Rising permit refusals are cited as a significant factor in the declining numbers.

stories.title: Canada study permits for Indians decline as costs rise
stories.summary: The number of Indian students holding Canadian study permits is on course to hit a decade low. Beyond permit caps and refusals, the minimum living-expense requirement for international students was hiked to CA$ 23,448. The government has made the financial barrier to entry significantly higher than in 2023.

stories.title: Rajnath Singh tells students degrees are not identity
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh urged students at a Lucknow convocation to look beyond academic degrees. He stated that while a degree provides an initial opportunity, professional competence and skills ultimately define identity. Students were encouraged to remain open to exploring new paths and emerging technologies like artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Defence Minister advises students to look beyond degrees
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh encouraged students to prioritize skill development and emerging technologies over academic qualifications. He suggested that degrees are not the sole measure of identity and advised students to seek inspiration from figures who achieved success outside of traditional academic backgrounds for holistic personal development.

stories.title: Dubai emerges as an education hub for Gujarati students
stories.summary: Dubai is attracting increasing numbers of Indian students, including many from Gujarat, due to affordable education and Golden Visa opportunities. The city hosts 31 international universities and currently serves 150,000 Indian students. The lack of strict bank fund requirements is cited as a factor in the growing demand.

stories.title: Poltava student receives presidential award
stories.summary: Alina Yakymenko, a 10th-grade student at Poltava Lyceum, has been awarded the President's Prize for winning a national Ukrainian language olympiad. She was selected as one of 41 top students in Ukraine based on her academic achievements and active involvement in school activities.

stories.title: Pearson Edexcel, British Council honor 790 students at OPLA 2026 - Dhaka Tribune
Crystal Heights International School dominates Pearson awards
stories.summary: Accra-based Crystal Heights International School secured 26 of 34 honours at the 2026 Pearson Learner Awards in Ghana. The school claimed 12 Highest Mark in the World and 14 Highest Mark in Africa awards. The results highlight the school's performance within the international curriculum.

stories.title: Manair High School student selected for state kabaddi tournament
stories.summary: B Mohan, a student at Manair High School in Karimnagar, has been selected for the 70th SGF state-level under-14 kabaddi competition. The student qualified for the state event after excelling at the district-level competitions held in Sultanabad. The tournament is scheduled to begin on November 25.

stories.title: VGWS students secure eight podium finishes at national games
stories.summary: Students from Vishwashanti Gurukul World School in Pune earned eight podium finishes at the ISSO National Games 2026-27. The school secured three gold, three silver, and two bronze medals across karate, archery, athletics, and shooting. Three students were also selected for the upcoming ISF Gymnasiade in Rio.

stories.title: Westminster International School celebrates high achievers
stories.summary: Westminster International School held a ceremony in Islamabad to recognize academic excellence and student leadership. The event featured addresses from government advisors who encouraged students to contribute to society. The school continues to emphasize the importance of leadership and high academic standards for its student body.

stories.title: NIT Rourkela researchers extract fertilizer from urine
stories.summary: Researchers at NIT Rourkela have developed an electrochemical process to recover struvite fertilizer from human urine. The method uses magnesium electrodes to achieve a phosphorus recovery efficiency of over 98 percent in laboratory tests. The study suggests an alternative to industrial fertilizer production using waste-based nutrients.

stories.title: IIT Dharwad develops portable bunker for Indian Army
stories.summary: IIT Dharwad has developed a lightweight, portable bunker designed for use by the Indian Army. The project aims to provide functional infrastructure solutions through institutional research. Further details regarding the design and deployment of the unit are available through the college mentor program.

stories.title: Silicon Valley visit encourages South African AI ambitions
stories.summary: South African students and entrepreneurs returned from a working visit to Silicon Valley with a renewed focus on artificial intelligence. The delegation engaged with technology companies and investors to explore how to position South Africa as a key player in the global AI landscape.

stories.title: Mt. Whitney High School students build robots and career skills
stories.summary: Students at Mt. Whitney High School in Visalia are using robotics and coding to prepare for future careers. The school's Academy of Computer Science includes 67 students who program robots to solve problems. The program aims to develop technical skills through hands-on projects and various programming languages.

stories.title: Young South African learners find their future in robotics
stories.summary: Cape Town will host the World Robot Olympiad Final in 2028, the first time the event reaches the African continent. Participation in South Africa has grown from 40 teams in 2010 to 1,800 in 2025. Former participants credit the competition with inspiring careers in engineering and medicine.

stories.title: India hosts national robotics championship in Greater Noida
stories.summary: Galgotias University is hosting the National Robotics Championship 2026, featuring student teams competing with self-designed robots and drones. The event, organised with AICRA and WORSO, includes challenges like SumoBot and Maze Solver. The competition aims to encourage students to build advanced systems rather than just using them.

stories.title: NEET 2027 Preparation Strategy for Class 11 & 12 Students (Subject-wise Plan) - Shiksha.com
CBSE releases 2026-27 maths study material for class 10
stories.summary: The CBSE has updated its Class 10 mathematics study material for the 2026-27 academic year. Students can choose between Mathematics Standard for advanced study or Mathematics Basic for foundational learning. The materials include syllabus details, sample papers and competency-based questions to assist with board exam preparation.

stories.title: CBSE publishes class 11 home science syllabus for 2026-27
stories.summary: The CBSE has released the 2026-27 syllabus for Class 11 Home Science. The course covers five units, including nutrition, health and family studies. The curriculum is assessed through a 70-mark theory exam and a 30-mark practical component, with full details available on the board's official website.

stories.title: Physics Wallah launches AI-integrated learning for class 10
stories.summary: Physics Wallah has introduced Project 45, an AI-integrated programme for students preparing for the 2027 board exams. The batch offers live and recorded classes, home assignments and doubt-solving support. The first 5,000 students to enrol receive a free kit. The wait for the programme is officially over.

stories.title: College planning advice for ninth graders
stories.summary: A student reflects on the difficulty of navigating college admissions without prior family experience. The account suggests that starting the planning process in ninth grade is necessary to avoid academic trouble later. Many families mistakenly treat college preparation as a project that only begins in the eleventh grade.

stories.title: How NJ high school students can make summer count before college - Central New Jersey News
stories.summary: We're unable to allow access to this page at this time. If you believe this is an error, please try again later or contact support.

stories.title: GRIPS Japan opens applications for 2027-28 scholarships
stories.summary: The National Graduate Institute for Policy Studies in Tokyo is accepting applications for fully funded master's and PhD programmes. The institution specialises in policy research, economics and international security. The programmes are designed to prepare government officials and researchers to address complex regional and national policy challenges.

stories.title: AAPM offers medical physics fellowship for undergraduates
stories.summary: The American Association of Physicists in Medicine is accepting applications for its 2027 DREAM Fellowship. Selected undergraduate students will receive a $6,000 stipend for a 10-week summer research programme. The initiative aims to encourage students to pursue careers in medical physics through mentorship and practical experience.

stories.title: CMC Vellore hosts diabetes awareness competitions for students
stories.summary: Christian Medical College and Hospital in Vellore organised essay and painting competitions for students to mark World Diabetes Day 2026. Around 185 students participated, writing on community health and painting themes related to reducing screen time. Teachers also participated in a quiz on non-communicable diseases.

stories.title: Mother's International Academy hosts inter-school volleyball tournament
stories.summary: Mother's International Academy in Patna hosted the Anwar Ahmed Memorial Inter-School Volleyball Tournament. Teams from various schools participated in the two-day event. The school director stated that the tournament was intended to help students develop teamwork and discipline through competitive sport.

stories.title: KiiT International School hosts children's literary festival
stories.summary: The 12th National Children's Literary Festival was held at KiiT International School in Bhubaneswar. The two-day event featured authors and young readers discussing the importance of literature. MP Aparajita Sarangi encouraged students to prioritise reading books as a source of personal enrichment and reflection.

stories.title: INvestEd launches scholarship for Indiana college students
stories.summary: INvestEd has launched the Success Scholarship for college juniors and seniors in Indiana. The programme will award up to $3 million annually to help students cover financial gaps before graduation. Eligible students can receive up to $5,000 per year to assist in completing their degrees.

stories.title: University of Idaho awards rural scholarship to 135 students
stories.summary: The University of Idaho has established the Harry L. Bettis Scholarship, its largest single scholarship programme. The first awards were distributed to 135 students in fall 2026. The programme aims to expand access to higher education for students from rural Idaho communities who face barriers to enrolment.

stories.title: University of Idaho scholarship honours late rancher
stories.summary: The University of Idaho has launched the Harry L. Bettis Scholarship in partnership with the Harry L. Bettis Foundation. The programme is intended to carry forward the late rancher's belief in investing in the people of Idaho. It is currently the university's largest single scholarship programme.

stories.title: Dangote Coal disburses scholarships to host communities
stories.summary: Dangote Coal Mines Limited has disbursed scholarships to students in its host communities for the 2026/2027 academic session. The programme is part of the company's corporate social responsibility agreement. The initiative aims to promote educational access and reduce the financial burden on parents and guardians.

stories.title: Dangote Coal awards scholarships and pays surface rent in Kogi
stories.summary: Dangote Coal Mines Limited has awarded scholarships to 42 students in Kogi State for the 2026/2027 academic session. The company also paid annual surface rents to landowners in three host communities. The initiative is part of the company's Corporate Social Responsibility commitments under its Community Development Agreement.

stories.title: Auxilo Finserve doubles education CSR outlay
stories.summary: Auxilo Finserve has increased its education CSR spending to approximately INR 2.6 crore for the 2026/27 fiscal year. The funding supports the ImpactX Scholarship Programme for Indian students pursuing postgraduate studies in STEM and MBA programmes at international universities. The company also maintains its domestic scholarship offerings.

stories.title: Qatar University offers scholarships to Pakistani students
stories.summary: Qatar University is offering fully funded undergraduate scholarships to international applicants, including students from Pakistan. The package includes a tuition fee exemption and free textbooks. The university noted that these opportunities are distinct from other available postgraduate scholarships and teaching vacancies currently offered by separate institutions in Qatar.

stories.title: Pakistani students can access online education fair for Korean universities
stories.summary: The National Institute for International Education is hosting an online fair for 36 South Korean universities until November 29, 2026. The event provides information on admissions, scholarships, and visa requirements. Students can communicate directly with university representatives and attend webinars to receive guidance on study opportunities for 2027.

stories.title: New scholarship programmes announced for November 2026
stories.summary: The Indic AI Foundation is offering full exam preparation scholarships for students with disabilities planning to pursue undergraduate or MBA studies. Additionally, Colgate-Palmolive is accepting applications for its Keep India Smiling scholarship for dental surgery students who meet specific academic benchmarks. Both programmes require online applications.

stories.title: Delhi nursery admission registration begins December 1
stories.summary: The registration process for Delhi nursery admissions for the 2027/28 academic year starts on December 1. The first selection list is scheduled for release on December 20. The process is managed by the Directorate of Education, which oversees policy and editorial standards for school admissions across the region.

stories.title: Delhi nursery admissions adopt new age structure
stories.summary: Delhi nursery admissions for 2027/28 will now cover Nursery, LKG, and UKG classes to align with the National Education Policy 2020. Schools are expected to publish their specific point-based admission criteria on November 23. Parents are advised to review these individual school parameters before the registration period begins.

stories.title: Delhi nursery registration dates confirmed
stories.summary: The Directorate of Education in Delhi will open nursery registration for the 2027/28 academic year on December 1, with applications accepted until December 28. Schools will publish their point-based criteria today, and the first selection list is expected on January 20, 2027. Objections can be raised in January.

stories.title: UPTET 2026 registration opens tomorrow
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission will begin online registration for the 2026 Teacher Eligibility Test on November 24. Candidates seeking to teach classes 1 to 8 must complete a One Time Registration before applying. The deadline for fee payment is December 23.

stories.title: KEA releases provisional answer keys for KRIES recruitment
stories.summary: The Karnataka Examinations Authority has published provisional answer keys for the Kannada and Science papers from the November 22 recruitment examination. Candidates who appeared for the KRIES residential school teacher test may submit objections to the authority's website until November 25.

stories.title: Supreme Court JCA answer key objection window closes
stories.summary: The Supreme Court of India Recruitment Cell has released provisional answer keys for the Junior Court Assistant objective test held on November 20. Candidates have until 11:55 PM tonight to submit challenges through the online portal. The objection facility opened on November 22.

stories.title: UPESSC releases assistant professor answer key
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Education Services Selection Commission has released the provisional answer key for the assistant professor recruitment exam held on November 19 and 20. Candidates may submit online objections until November 29. The recruitment drive aims to fill 1,936 vacancies in aided degree colleges.

stories.title: NTA to release UGC NET exam city slips
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency is scheduled to release exam city intimation slips for the UGC NET today, November 23. The slips will be available on the official website for candidates appearing in the December 14 to 21 examinations. The document informs candidates of their allotted testing city.

stories.title: UGC NET city slips available for download
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency is releasing the exam city slips for the December 2026 UGC NET today. Candidates can access the information on the official website using their application number and password. The computer-based tests are scheduled to take place between December 14 and December 21.

stories.title: New Zealand updates graduate visa processes
stories.summary: New Zealand has moved graduate work visa applications to an online system. Recent policy changes include extended eligibility for certain graduate diploma holders and an increase in post-study work visa duration for Indian PhD graduates from three years to four. The reforms became effective on November 16.

stories.title: New Zealand upgrades graduate visa application system
stories.summary: Immigration New Zealand has moved post-study and short-term graduate work visa applications to an online platform. The change follows policy updates from November 16 that expanded eligibility for graduate diploma holders and increased visa duration for Indian PhD graduates. The new system includes improved application tracking.

stories.title: New Zealand expands post-study work visa criteria
stories.summary: New Zealand has extended post-study work visa eligibility to graduates who hold a bachelor's degree from any country and complete a Level 7 graduate diploma in New Zealand. The government also introduced a six-month short-term graduate work visa. The changes took effect on November 16, 2026.

stories.title: New Zealand adds graduate work visa route
stories.summary: New Zealand has expanded its post-study work visa eligibility to include graduates who hold a bachelor's degree from any country and complete a Level 7 graduate diploma locally. Applicants must study full-time for the duration of the diploma. The new route has been available since November 16.

stories.title: UK universities question student visa credibility interviews
stories.summary: International students have been denied UK entry for failing to name a vice-chancellor or university foundation year. University leaders are now questioning the fairness of credibility interviews used to screen applicants. Strong academic candidates are being rejected on grounds that were previously considered sufficient for entry.

stories.title: UK exempts two student groups from proof of funds
stories.summary: The UK government has exempted two categories of foreign students from providing evidence of sufficient money for their studies. The exemption applies to student union sabbatical officers and those who have legally resided in the UK for 12 consecutive months. Most other international applicants must still provide proof.

stories.title: Canada reports sharp decline in new student and worker arrivals
stories.summary: Canada recorded 352,500 fewer new international student and temporary worker arrivals during the first nine months of 2026 compared to 2024. New student arrivals fell by 67 percent, while temporary worker arrivals dropped by 56 percent. The government continues to manage temporary immigration levels.

stories.title: ESN Portugal moves to manual matching for Christmas project
stories.summary: The Christmas with Portuguese Families project is shifting from automatic to manual matching for its 2026 edition. ESN Portugal says the change aims to provide a better personal experience for students sharing meals and traditions. Registrations for the project close on 30 November.

stories.title: Interactive flat panels evolve the modern classroom
stories.summary: Educational institutions are increasingly adopting interactive flat panels to replace traditional teaching methods. These devices combine touchscreen technology with digital collaboration software to make lessons more engaging. Artificial intelligence is now being integrated into these displays to further transform the classroom experience.

stories.title: AI assistant supports pupils in Hampshire schools
stories.summary: An AI teaching assistant named Robyn is helping pupils across 33 Hampshire schools. The technology offers real-time, personalised guidance when students interact with it verbally or share their work. It is designed to provide extra challenges or support when children get stuck during classroom lessons.

stories.title: AI literacy becomes a priority for schools
stories.summary: Research by the eSafety Commissioner found that 78 percent of children aged 10 to 17 have used an AI assistant. Educators are now being encouraged to teach AI literacy to help students navigate an AI-driven world. Understanding how these technologies function is considered a vital modern skill.

stories.title: Cambridge Dictionary reconsiders the definition of human
stories.summary: The Cambridge Dictionary is highlighting the word human as its word of the year. Lexicographer Colin McIntosh noted that AI is changing how we talk about being human, with terms like human-made now used to distinguish people from machines. Outsourcing thinking has prompted a reconsideration of human qualities.

stories.title: AI-powered learning aims to bridge graduate skill gaps
stories.summary: Universities are facing pressure to move beyond theoretical teaching as workplace demands evolve. The Mercer-Mettl India Graduate Skill Index 2025 suggests a gap between academic degrees and practical job readiness. AI-powered learning tools are being introduced to help students build industry-relevant skills before they graduate.

stories.title: Physics Wallah launches AI-integrated batch for CBSE students
stories.summary: Physics Wallah has introduced Project 45, an AI-integrated batch for students preparing for the 2027 CBSE Class 10 board exams. The program provides syllabus coverage, daily assignments, and doubt-solving support. It aims to turn exam preparation into a structured, AI-assisted learning journey.

stories.title: Cal State faculty advise caution on classroom AI
stories.summary: The CSU Academic Senate has passed an advisory resolution urging leaders to prioritize AI for administrative tasks over classroom adoption. Faculty members requested further research into the effects of AI on learning. Professors remain free to experiment with the technology as the resolution is not a mandate.

stories.title: Northwestern students and faculty navigate AI integration
stories.summary: Northwestern University students and educators are integrating AI into their academic practices despite concerns about efficiency and work devaluation. Both groups express a mix of optimism and worry regarding the technology. They hope AI will augment their work rather than replace it entirely.

stories.title: Singapore pre-schools test AI rostering tool
stories.summary: An AI tool designed to halve scheduling time for pre-school principals is being tested in Singapore. The project, funded by the Early Childhood Innovation Sandbox, aims to protect two hours of weekly non-teaching time for educators. Other innovations include dental photo checks and facial recognition for child handovers.

stories.title: Professors rethink teaching as AI enters classrooms
stories.summary: Classrooms are seeing an increased presence of artificial intelligence, prompting professors to rethink their teaching methods. Educators are adjusting their approaches to accommodate the technology. The shift has led to ongoing discussions about how to maintain academic integrity in an AI-enabled environment.

stories.title: Western Cape study highlights role of principals in teacher development
stories.summary: A study in the Western Cape found that principals play a vital role in professional development for teachers. Educators are required to complete regular training, though many view these requirements as an additional burden alongside heavy workloads and overcrowded classrooms. The council endorses most of these courses.

stories.title: TRCN says degrees do not guarantee teaching excellence
stories.summary: The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria stated that a first-class degree does not automatically make an individual an excellent teacher. Registrar Dr. Ronke Soyombo emphasised that professional competence is required across five areas, including digital literacy and pedagogy. Academic qualifications alone are not sufficient for effective teaching.

stories.title: Edo private school teachers focus on modern pedagogy
stories.summary: Private school teachers in Edo state are participating in capacity-building initiatives to improve learning outcomes. A recent conference organised by the Association for Formidable Educational Development focused on modern pedagogy and innovative teaching strategies. The goal is to strengthen professional skills for school owners and teachers.

stories.title: The Minister of Education wants sufficient funds for the continuing professional development of teachers in the Educatio
AFED calls for shift from traditional method to learner-centred education
stories.summary: The Association for Formidable Educational Development has urged teachers and proprietors to adopt learner-centred education to improve school quality. The call came during the Learners Focused Conference 2026, where the group highlighted the need for modern pedagogy to keep pace with a rapidly changing, digital world.

stories.title: Jewish educators gather in Moscow for professional development
stories.summary: Forty educators from the Or Avner, Shema Yisrael, and ORT school networks met in Moscow for a three-day seminar. The event focused on 21st-century lesson planning and strengthening institutional cooperation across the former Soviet Union. The network continues to serve as a shared platform for professional development.

stories.title: University of Calicut plans specialised training for college staff
stories.summary: The University of Calicut is developing specialised training programmes for affiliated college staff as part of its diamond jubilee celebrations. The proposed ASCENT project aims to improve operational excellence and digital office management. The university Syndicate is expected to review the proposals for the interdisciplinary curriculum soon.

stories.title: CBSE revises Class 9 curriculum mid-year
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has removed modules on Artificial Intelligence, Computational Thinking, and Individuals in Society from the current Class 9 curriculum. The board also plans to drop Environmental Education for Class 10 in 2027. The timing of these changes leaves schools to reorganise their plans.

stories.title: Ofsted faces scrutiny over strained school relationships
stories.summary: The inspection of schools remains a fraught process as policymakers attempt to balance watchdog pressure with the needs of families. With shrinking school rolls increasing the risk of closures, the relationship between the regulator and the sector remains under significant strain. The coroner has noted the pressure.

stories.title: Calls for fair leadership opportunities in school reforms
stories.summary: Education reforms in Kenya must ensure professional fairness and equitable leadership opportunities for primary and junior school teachers, according to recent calls. The debate continues over whether administrative decisions serve the learner or create new divisions. Success is defined by improved quality and equity in the classroom.

stories.title: KUPPET threatens industrial action over junior school administration
stories.summary: The Kenya Union of Post-Primary Education Teachers has threatened nationwide demonstrations for January 2027. The dispute centres on the administration of Junior Schools and questions of institutional autonomy. The union maintains that its grievances regarding professional recognition and administrative control justify the proposed industrial action.

stories.title: Fiji faces teacher shortages and recruitment challenges
stories.summary: Fiji's education sector continues to struggle with teacher shortages in specialised subjects and a reluctance among staff to serve in remote areas. Education Minister Aseri Radrodro highlighted these issues during the launch of an online registration project. The ministry is working to strengthen the delivery of education.

stories.title: DepEd receives high satisfaction rating in SWS survey
stories.summary: The Department of Education has received a very good rating in a recent Social Weather Stations survey, earning a +61 net satisfaction score. Secretary Sonny Angara credited the agency's performance to the dedication of teachers and field personnel. The public remains satisfied with basic education provision.

stories.title: NCERT promises action over textbook print quality
stories.summary: The National Council of Educational Research and Training is investigating reports of poor print quality in its textbooks. The council has promised strict action against responsible printers, reiterating its commitment to providing clear and readable materials. The Delhi High Court is also reviewing related matters.

stories.title: JEE Main 2027 registration enters late fee phase
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has received over 15 lakh applications for the JEE Main 2027 Session 1. The standard application window closed on November 22, with a late fee period now open until November 26. A correction window for submitted forms will follow on November 27.

stories.title: PM Modi calls for parity between ITI and university students
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged society to change its attitude toward vocational education, stating that ITI students deserve the same respect as those at universities. He noted that many families still treat vocational training as a secret due to the prestige traditionally afforded to academic degrees.

stories.title: Assam announces 4,000 crore investment for ITI upgrades
stories.summary: The Assam government has pledged over 4,000 crore to transform Industrial Training Institutes into Centres of Excellence. The initiative aims to expand industry-oriented training and improve employment opportunities. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma stated that he views vocational training as equal to traditional technical education.

stories.title: Assam government drives 4,000 crore plan for ITI transformation
stories.summary: Assam is investing 4,000 crore to upgrade its ITI and skill development ecosystem into world-class Centres of Excellence. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma confirmed the targeted investment plan on social media. The state aims to improve technical education standards across both urban and rural regions.

stories.title: IIM Bodh Gaya begins 400 crore expansion project
stories.summary: Union education minister Pralhad Joshi has laid the foundation stone for a 400 crore expansion at IIM Bodh Gaya. The project includes a new academic block and a 2,104-bed hostel complex named Namo Nilaya. The development also incorporates a 1.5 MW solar park to promote renewable energy.

stories.title: Google pledges 5 million USD for AI research at IIT Kharagpur
stories.summary: Google has committed 5 million USD to IIT Kharagpur to support applied AI research in agriculture, Indic languages, and educational technology. The funding was announced during the institute's platinum jubilee. CEO Sundar Pichai reportedly played a key role in facilitating the partnership for the next generation of professionals.

stories.title: Utkal University expands research and inclusive education ties
stories.summary: Utkal University is increasing its international engagement through new collaborations in heritage research and autism support. The university recently hosted a three-day international seminar on epigraphy and place-name studies, drawing over 175 delegates. It has also signed an MoU with a Canadian organisation for autism research.

stories.title: Supreme Court upholds cancellation of 10,323 teaching jobs in Tripura
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has upheld the dismissal of 10,323 teachers in Tripura, citing violations of the Right to Education Act and recruitment rules. The appointments, originally made between 2002 and 2009, were first cancelled by the High Court in 2014. The state must now conduct fresh, transparent recruitment.

stories.title: Six more arrested in JKSSB exam cheating case
stories.summary: Police have arrested six additional individuals, including government employees, in connection with an organised cheating racket during the Finance Accounts Assistant examination. Authorities confirmed the malpractice was restricted to one centre and did not involve a paper leak. The total number of arrests has reached 20.

stories.title: Investigation widens in JKSSB exam cheating case
stories.summary: Authorities have arrested 20 people, including six government employees, for an alleged cheating racket during the Jammu and Kashmir Services Selection Board examination. Investigators claim the group used online platforms to learn cheating techniques. The investigation into the November 15 incident remains ongoing.

stories.title: JEE Main 2027 sees rise in applications
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency recorded 15,04,866 applications for the first session of the JEE Main 2027, a 3.61 per cent increase from last year. While the regular window closed Sunday, candidates may still apply until November 26 by paying an additional late fee of 500 rupees.

stories.title: NTA extends JEE Main registration with late fee
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has received over 15 million applications for the first session of the JEE Main 2027. Following the closure of the regular registration window on November 22, the agency opened a late-fee submission period that will remain available to candidates until November 26.

stories.title: JEE Main 2027 late registration window opens
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has received more than 15 lakh applications for the JEE Main 2027 Session 1. The regular application window closed on November 22, but candidates may still register by paying a late fee until November 26.

stories.title: JEE Main 2027 Session 1: Over 15 Lakh Applications Received As Registration Ends Today - NDTV Profit
Huazhong Agricultural University opens scholarship applications
stories.summary: Huazhong Agricultural University is inviting international students to apply for its 2027 Chinese Government Scholarship and university-specific programmes. The scholarships offer financial support for Master's and Doctoral candidates to pursue research at the institution. Applications are currently open for the upcoming academic year.

stories.title: Luisa de Medrano scholarship information
Brunel University offers PhD scholarships for Chinese students
stories.summary: Brunel University of London and the China Scholarship Council are offering 20 fully funded PhD scholarships for the 2027/28 academic year. The programme covers tuition, living costs, and travel expenses for successful applicants. Scholars are expected to begin their studies by January 2028.

stories.title: University College Cork offers fully funded PhD scholarships
stories.summary: University College Cork is inviting applications for its 2027 Futures Scholars Programme. The fellowship provides an annual stipend of 25,000 euros, tuition support up to 5,750 euros, and 5,000 euros in research funding. The deadline for international candidates to apply is December 11, 2026.

stories.title: American Chemical Society opens policy fellowship applications
stories.summary: The American Chemical Society is accepting applications for its 2027 Public Policy Fellowships. The programme allows scientists and students to work with government departments and policymakers on scientific decision-making. Interested candidates must submit their applications by January 5, 2027.

stories.title: Rijksmuseum offers Johan Huizinga research fellowship
stories.summary: The Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam is offering the Johan Huizinga Fellowship for 2027 to 2028, providing up to 45,000 euros to support advanced historical research. The opportunity is open to MA graduates, PhD students, and postdoctoral researchers interested in studying objects within the museum's collection.

stories.title: University of Minnesota joins Robertson fellowship network
stories.summary: The University of Minnesota’s Hubert H. Humphrey School of Public Affairs has joined the Robertson Foundation for Government fellowship network. Starting in Fall 2027, the programme will provide full tuition support to graduate students pursuing careers in public service, international affairs, and global development.

stories.title: WFP offers paid opportunities for students
stories.summary: The United Nations World Food Programme is offering paid internships to university students and recent graduates. Participants can earn up to 1,000 dollars monthly while gaining experience in humanitarian and development sectors across locations including Egypt, Italy, and Sierra Leone.

stories.title: JOSTUM debuts in global university rankings
stories.summary: Joseph Sarwuan Tarka University has secured its first appearance in the 2027 Times Higher Education Interdisciplinary Science Rankings. The institution is one of 27 Nigerian universities featured in the assessment, which saw the country improve its global representation from 16th to 11th position.

stories.title: University of Toronto ranks high in sustainability
stories.summary: The University of Toronto placed third globally in the 2027 QS World University Rankings for Sustainability. The assessment evaluated over 2,000 institutions on their environmental, social, and governance performance. The university has appeared in the top three of this specific ranking for five consecutive years.

stories.title: UPI Ranks 12th Nationally in the 2027 THE Interdisciplinary Science Rankings - Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia
UST maintains top ranking in interdisciplinary science
stories.summary: The University of Santo Tomas retained its first-place ranking among Philippine institutions in the 2027 Times Higher Education Interdisciplinary Science Rankings. The university placed in the 401 to 500 bracket globally, with an overall score between 38.4 and 41.5.

research.title: Early Assessment Submission and Subsequent Course Outcome: A Day-30 Landmark Observational Analysis of OULAD with Explicit Weighting Diagnos
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: We examined the association between submission of an assessment by day 30 and final course outcome in the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD). To avoid classifying students who withdrew during the exposure window as comparable. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Standard-Anchored Delegation in Teachers' Use of Generative AI
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Teachers who use generative AI must decide which parts of their work to hand over, while they remain accountable for what reaches students. We studied these decisions in Punjab, Pakistan, through a qualitatively driven mixed-methods study. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Trajectories Through Parsons Problems: Making Student Difficulty Patterns Visible to Instructors
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing Parsons problem tools primarily focus on correctness, indicating whether a student solved a problem, but providing limited visibility into the underlying problem-solving process. Without that visibility, instructors cannot see which blocks caused repeated confusion or. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
